    • removeSupersededSnapshotBuild

      public static boolean removeSupersededSnapshotBuild(Path buildRoot) throws IOException
      Deletes the test build of a version once that version has been built as a release.

      A "Rebuild only" run names its folder after the current version, including -SNAPSHOT (e.g. Glyco-PAINT-0.0.138-SNAPSHOT). Once the release folder Glyco-PAINT-0.0.138 exists, that test build is superseded and only confusing. Does nothing if buildRoot is itself a SNAPSHOT build, or if there is no test build.

      Parameters:
      buildRoot - the folder just built, e.g. .../Glyco-PAINT-Builds/Glyco-PAINT-0.0.138
      Returns:
      true if a superseded SNAPSHOT folder was deleted
      Throws:
      IOException - if the folder exists but cannot be deleted

    • requireArtifact

      public static Path requireArtifact(Path dir, String fileName) throws IOException
      Resolves exactly one expected build artifact, by name.

      This deliberately replaces an earlier "newest file matching a loose pattern" lookup. A Maven target directory does not hold one candidate: maven-shade-plugin leaves the pre-shade jar behind as original-<name>.jar alongside the real, shaded one. A pattern such as .*jar$ matches both, and picking the most recently modified one is a race — shade writes them within milliseconds of each other. Losing that race means shipping a thin, non-runnable jar under the official release name.

      Artifact names are deterministic, so ask for the one we mean and fail loudly if it is not there.

      Parameters:
      dir - the directory to look in (typically a module's target)
      fileName - the exact name expected, e.g. paint-installer-macos-1.2.3.jar, or a macOS app bundle (a folder) such as Glyco-PAINT.app
      Returns:
      the path to that artifact
      Throws:
      IOException - if it does not exist, listing what the directory does contain
